title: Finiteness via properness and finite fibres over a locally Noetherian base: for f : X -> S with S locally Noetherian, f is finite if and only if f is proper with finite fibres (retained with the author's parenthetical pointing to the more general More on Morphisms twin).

core_obligations: Prove the forward direction by composing finite-proper and finite-quasi-finite.
Reduce the converse to affineness through the integral-plus-proper criterion.
Apply the H^1-vanishing affine criterion to finite type ideal sheaves on X.
Kill R^1f_* via finite fibres and descend through Leray to the affine base.

proof_roadmap.step: Prove the forward direction by composing finite-proper and finite-quasi-finite.
Reduce the converse to affineness through the integral-plus-proper criterion.
Apply the H^1-vanishing affine criterion to finite type ideal sheaves on X.

difficulty_reason: Both directions are argued in the span: finite implies proper and quasi-finite (hence finite fibres) by the two Morphisms-chapter lemmas composed in prose; conversely, assuming proper with finite fibres, it suffices to prove affineness because an affine integral universally closed morphism is integral and a proper integral morphism is finite (the chain is spelled out); affineness is local on S, so take S affine and apply this chapter's affine criterion lemma-quasi-separated-h1-zero-covering: for a finite type ideal sheaf I on X, coherence lets the finite-fibre direct-image vanishing give R^1f_*I = 0, the Leray spectral sequence turns H^1(X, I) into H^1(S, f_*I), and affineness of S kills the latter since f_*I is quasi-coherent (schemes-push-forward-quasi-coherent plus the affine vanishing lemma).
